elevations.notes: Physical east to west: salmon Brummer14 (7upperaxes), yellow Remander16 (7axes perupperrow, middle3pediments, asymmetric currentground openings), offwhite Sederholm18 (7upperaxes, whitepilasters/balustrades). Street View plus official architectural photograph establish distinct layouts. Clear April2023 Brummer panorama resolves five shuttered ground windows and two doors (eastmost and centre); current asymmetric Remander ground is retained rather than copied from2005.

limitations: Only the north square-facing plane is restored. Long Katariinankatu west elevation, roofs and all courtyard wings retain their original municipal materials.
The source municipal mesh has no vertical central north Sederholm gable above its flat eave. A material chart cannot recreate the missing projecting pediment; it is not painted over the top windows.
Window and masonry dimensions are original authored approximations fitted to exact municipal source planes.

elevations.notes: Four opening axes on both upper rows, narrow barred lower windows. West wing is physically set back from the projecting central portico. Upper wall is warm desaturated pink/sandstone behind cream columns/pilasters; rusticated ground remains cream above gray-brown granite plinth, matched to opened Street View.

Six fluted Corinthian columns, five upper opening axes, three ornate central ground doors and the raised plinth balustrade. Upper wall is warm desaturated pink/sandstone behind cream columns/pilasters; rusticated ground remains cream above gray-brown granite plinth, matched to opened Street View.

Four upper axes. Source main wall is set back separately from the central portico. Upper wall is warm desaturated pink/sandstone behind cream columns/pilasters; rusticated ground remains cream above gray-brown granite plinth, matched to opened Street View.

limitations: Only the three directly observed south front planes are restored. Unobserved side, rear, roof, and narrow inset returns retain municipal source materials.
Column shafts, capitals and balustrade are original flat artwork on the unchanged source wall plane, without added projecting geometry.
Opening dimensions and vertical positions are approximate; street-level alignment requires final runtime confirmation.

elevations.notes: Five horizontal glazing levels: glazed ground floor plus four upper ribbons; original narrow metal mullions and finely grooved offwhite spandrels.
Left courtyard wing, continuous horizontal glazing and offwhite spandrels.
Low glazed east pavilion with green metal framing and copper-green roof fascia.
Five continuous ribbon-window rows directly observed in upward panorama; offwhite small rectangular tile/grid spandrels, flat roof coping, ground-level black slat grille.
Separate recessed full-height glass zone: five glazed floors, dark opaque spandrels, blue-green original reflection gradient. Ground glazing has a black vertical slat grille.
South zone adjacent to glass inset is observed blank offwhite rectangular tile on upper three floors. No openings invented; lower unconfirmed area receives only the same original neutral material.

limitations: Observed public south courtyard and three separately matched eastern source wall zones are restored; outer north and west, roofs, low east street return and unobserved courtyard returns retain original municipal materials.
Narrow glazing subdivisions are authored approximations of the observed continuous ribbon construction, not a surveyed pane count.
Source geometry and all terraces and stairs remain unchanged.
